author: Warren Buffett
title: Warren Buffett’s Thanksgiving Letter to Shareholders
headline: Warren Buffett is “going quiet”: Greg Abel takes over at year-end, and Buffett speeds up gifts of his Berkshire shares to his children’s foundations.
summary: At 95, Buffett tells shareholders he will stop writing the annual report and talking at the annual meeting, but will keep sending a Thanksgiving message. Greg Abel becomes CEO at year-end, and Buffett cannot think of anyone he would rather have handle their savings. He converted 1,800 A shares into 2.7 million B shares for four family foundations and will speed up lifetime gifts, while keeping a significant amount of A shares until shareholders are as comfortable with Abel as they were with him and Charlie Munger. He sees moderately better-than-average prospects for Berkshire, but expects many companies to do better as its size takes its toll.

takeaways.label: Move
takeaways.text: Converted 1,800 A shares into 2.7 million B shares and gave them to four family foundations; gifts to his children’s foundations will speed up.

takeaways.label: View
takeaways.text: The faster giving says nothing about Berkshire’s prospects: Greg Abel has more than met Buffett’s high expectations.

takeaways.label: View
takeaways.text: Prospects are moderately better than average, led by a few sizable gems, but in a decade or two many companies will have done better than Berkshire.

takeaways.label: View
takeaways.text: With Berkshire’s size and today’s market levels, ideas are few, but not zero.

takeaways.label: Watch
takeaways.text: Buffett keeps a significant amount of A shares until shareholders trust Abel as they trusted him and Munger.

risks.text: The share price will move capriciously and can fall 50% or so, as it has three times in 60 years.
A loyal CEO of the parent or a subsidiary may succumb to dementia or another long illness; Buffett and Munger failed to act several times.

quotes.text: As the British would say, I’m “going quiet.”
I can’t think of a CEO, a management consultant, an academic, a member of government – you name it – that I would select over Greg to handle your savings and mine.
Our stock price will move capriciously, occasionally falling 50% or so as has happened three times in 60 years under present management.

stocks.note: Moderately better-than-average prospects; less risk of disaster than any business Buffett knows.
